questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was keen on moving to Italy. I love the language, the cuisine and pretty much all of the Italian culture. I have been studying Italian language at my gymnasium, and I thought that a exchange program in Italy could be an opportunity to talk and learn more Italian.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy due to the fact that the coordinator in Milan was very nice, responding to email quickly and so forth. There were also an orientation meeting held by students where we got information of more social character.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Massimo Costa, the coordinator, was of great assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was not "on" campus in the sense that the campus i was living at, "Campus Martinitt", was not situated by the place we studied. On Campus Martinitt you got a shared room (1 roommate). And I think it was possible to apply for different campuses.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Common cooking area - very nice. You have to bring and keep your own tools, pans etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is super nice and cheap. I think it is a nice way to get to know other exchange students as well as locals.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to go to a office within certain time slots and wait until Massimo registers you. Then you get a document you have to save until you leave again, and you get your student-id.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Personal guidance from Massimo.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration for courses was nice. Only thing is that many courses have lectures at the same time during the week, so to coordinate your schedule and get all the courses you want is almost impossible.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask Massimo as much you can if in doubt.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level is not to high. At least the exams are not that difficult compared to UCPH.
But if you want, you can get a great experience due to the nice professors and interesting topics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH it was not nearly as interactive - there were less questions and cases. The exam form was predominantly oral.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Law and history
Roman Law
European monetary and economic law
Refugee protection
Competition law

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: European monetary law and Roman law. These topics were both well taught and very interesting. On UCPH we don't have lessons regarding the EURO-currency and the legal framework in that regard, even though our own currency is greatly affected by it. And compared to the law history course we have on UCPH, this Roman Law course is way more advanced and the professor is fluent in latin.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected and so was the restaurants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was mostly on my campus (where i lived) - parties. But I know that it was possible to go on trips etc. with the erasmus community.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Live at a campus (housing through the university)!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Milan is located very central in the northern part of Italy, so it is easy to take train other cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Milan is very european and reminds me a lot of Copenhagen actually, people really live and work in the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go talk to them. They were way more open than I expected.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love Italians approach to food, wine and other life quality enhancing concepts.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to meet locals and other exchange students,
enjoy the city there are a lot of cafés, restaurants and so a like,
and relax with regards to the courses - the exams are not as difficult as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social part. I think living at the campus Martinitt

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The change of scenery - meeting new people, waking up in a new bed and so on.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
